items.title: 68089_John Malachi oral history interview
items.q: he would ask me sometimes if I would go down and play with them for an hour... a saxophone player, I remember his last name was Winbush

ctx.x: lot of pieces I really learned just from ear.

So before long, to make a long story short, being a professional musician himself, he was playing at a little I guess you'd call it club down on E Street between 10th and 11th Street. It was upstairs; I never will remember the name. But he was working with two other musicians, a saxophone player, I remember his last name was Winbush, and there was a drummer, his name was Eugene Carroll. I guess I must have been about just turned at my 15th birthday. My teacher was working with these guys, and he would ask me…

Well, the whole idea of me sitting there and playing with grown men really made... Like any kid who can do something along with grown men, it makes you feel pretty good if you like what you're doing. So I was very grateful. I learned later that in this hour he would have maybe another job that he was playing, or maybe he'd give a piano lesson or something. I don't know what'all he did. But he had me to substitute for him for that hour, which I never got any money
